name: local-liveflags-replay
status: kept diagnostic; local green at 100k, relay cliff above 100k
hypothesis: The latest local harness should recover item219/item251-class throughput when run with the same Mahi live flags used by Ansible. A no-live-flags run is expected to be misleading because it does not exercise observer async owner relay or peer transport.

results.label: no-live-flags-100k
results.classification: fail mode; local harness omitted live Mahi flags and hit local_submit_queue_full

results.label: liveflags-100k-green
results.classification: success mode; latest code is locally green when run with live-equivalent Mahi flags

results.label: liveflags-120k-relay-cliff
results.classification: fail mode; ingress accepted load but owner-relay drain stalled

results.label: liveflags-150k-relay-cliff
results.classification: fail mode; sharper owner-relay drain stall above 120k

decision.status: kept diagnostic; local green artifact retained
decision.reason: The local code path is healthy at 100k when live flags are present. Above 100k, the bottleneck is not public ingress acceptance or commit correctness; it is pending Mahi owner-relay drain from observer to validators.
decision.next_move: Do not tune consensus from the no-live-flags result. Use the 100k liveflags artifact as the local green baseline. If optimizing locally, target owner-relay drain instrumentation/transport before attempting another >100k run.
